title: The program it writes, and the design at its end
summary: One .rex file is both the program and the design. It holds: a UserDialog subclass whose defineDialog makes the controls with createXxx and connects events with connectXxxEvent; one UNGUARDED accessor per control (self~lcd~setText(x)); one method per event named on_<control>_<event> holding the user's code (the form's OK and CANCEL override ok and cancel); the form's variables as ::attribute; the form's own methods; generated helpers (<tab>_pageChanged, <tab>_show, timer_<t>, and for bound dialogs <ctl>_bound, <list>_load/_save/_add/_remove); ::routines; ::RESOURCE strings.<language> when translatable; and last ::RESOURCE oodDesign, the design as lines (form, control, prop, event, binding ...). Open... reads the design back from the resource and the event code from the methods.
invariants: Round trip is byte-identical: generate, read back, generate again gives the same file (t01, t03, t10 check it).
Whatever lies between the last event method and the next directive is read back as that method's code: a generated ::routine keeps its comment inside the routine, never before it.
Generated code uses only documented upstream ooDialog API so it runs on Windows ooDialog unchanged.
Every generated method is UNGUARDED, as the ooDialog guide asks of event handlers.
Background events reply at once (after EXPOSE, which must come first).
